unfair: Arm V's screenshots reach the model in two steps: the stock harness puts an MCP tool's image into the conversation only while it is tiny (base64 under about 10 to 16 KB, measured); a larger one, which is every useful render (a 256 px solid view of a cube is 53 KB), is saved to a file and the path returned ('[Resource offloaded to file:///...media_0.png]'), and the agent sees the picture only if it opens that file with view_file (tests/test_compare_agents.py). That is the stock agent's behaviour with any MCP server and is left as it is; each V record counts screenshots taken and opened.

Arm V's Blender has a virtual display (Xvfb) inside the sandbox, because its screenshot is Blender's solid-viewport renderer (Workbench), which needs OpenGL: without a display Blender 5.3 exits at the first render (measured). Arm A's Blender has none, as in round 3; Cycles works without one.

Arm V's Blender binary is mounted in the sandbox (the MCP server starts it) but is not on PATH and not named in its task; an agent that finds it can still run it from the shell. Each record counts shell commands that start Blender (blender_invocations), so a V run that bypassed its MCP server is visible.

Arms V and A run with 0 images: the owner's image allowance is used up (29 of 30), and the relay refuses an image call. A stock agent made no image in round 3 (its textures were procedural); the task text is unchanged.
Arms N and C make their textures as images and are not run until the owner allows more images.

Arm C is told less than the agents: its command line carries the brief, engine and triangle budget, but not the rest of the game-ready list (C_UNEXPRESSED); the pipeline applies its own conventions there.

Arm C's change request is `agy3d edit OUT "<change>"` on a copy of its first output folder: one patch to the shipped design, no image (C_CHANGE_MODE; 'append', a new design from the sentence appended to the prompt, is kept for comparison). The agents' change sessions are new conversations over the files their first session left.

Every arm's task ends with a budget sentence ('about N model calls'), N computed from its share (CALL_MODEL); maxOutputTokens is 16,384 instead of the stock 65,535; web search and URL reading are disabled (no network).

The upstream qa_check / mesh_stats / texel_density scripts are by the author of the skills arm B used (round 1). The Godot import script and the three.js check are this project's own (C's authors); they are applied to the bare GLB of every arm with a manifest holding only the bounds read from that GLB.
The judge is Gemini (gemini-4-carbon, thinking low) judging Gemini-made assets; renders are Blender's (Cycles), not the target engine's.

Rows that only this project can pass are marked so in the scorecard (installed into a project, provenance, the same bytes from the same request): they are reported, not mixed into the shared game-ready rate.
The machine is shared: other test suites may run on its 4 cores during live runs; each record carries the load at its start and end. Wall times are not comparable with an idle machine.
